Estimates of reproductive output in the Darkedge midshipman, Porichthys analis, have been derived from comparative data on its congener, Porichthys notatus, which exhibits similar egg characteristics. Based on an average egg diameter of 0.47 centimeters, the calculated wet weight of a single egg is approximately 0.0544 grams [Wwb = approximately 0.0544 grams], a figure that reflects the considerable yolk investment typical of demersal spawners. Field observations indicate that females attain sexual maturity upon reaching a total length of 15.7 centimeters [Lp = 15.7 centimeters], a milestone associated with the onset of gonadal recrudescence. At this size, the corresponding wet weight at puberty has been documented at roughly 40.5 grams [Wwp = roughly 40.5 grams], placing this species in a moderate size range among nearshore batrachoidids. The transition from an endotrophic yolk-sac larva to an exotrophic juvenile represents a critical period, and the substantial per-offspring investment implied by the egg mass likely contributes to higher early-stage survival rates in this vocalizing fish.

The maximum body size recorded for female Darkedge midshipman has been established at a total length of 36 centimeters [Li = 36 centimeters], a value that results in an estimated ultimate wet weight of approximately 553 grams [Wwi = approximately 553 grams] when applying the length-weight relationship derived for this lineage. This asymptotic mass is notably larger than the mass at puberty, indicating a prolonged period of post-maturational somatic growth common among iteroparous teleosts. The pronounced size discrepancy between these life stages suggests that females continue to allocate resources toward structural growth well after the onset of reproductive activity, a pattern that may be linked to the selective pressures of nest guarding and acoustic communication in this species. The relationship between length and mass in P. analis follows the general batrachoidid form, with weight increasing as a power function of length. Adult males are known to produce characteristic hums and grunts to attract gravid females to nesting sites, making body size a potential factor in both acoustic signal strength and competitive success.

Reproductive frequency in the Darkedge midshipman has been extrapolated from fecundity data in the closely related plainfin midshipman, Porichthys notatus. Available information suggests that a female produces approximately 110 eggs per spawning event and likely completes just one spawning event per year, yielding a maximum daily reproduction rate of approximately 0.3 offspring per day [Ri = approximately 0.3 offspring per day] under controlled thermal conditions. The single annual reproductive bout, combined with a moderate clutch size and substantial per-egg investment, aligns with a life history strategy oriented toward offspring quality rather than maximal numerical output. These patterns were assessed at a stable water temperature of 18.5 °C [T = 18.5 °C], a regime that supports normal metabolic function and gonadal development in this species. The seasonal timing of spawning is likely cued by photoperiod and temperature fluctuations along the Pacific coast.

Longevity data for Porichthys analis have been gathered from both captive rearing studies and mark-recapture efforts in its natural habitat. The maximum lifespan of this species has been recorded at 9 years [am = 9 years] under controlled aquarium conditions at a water temperature of 18.5 °C [T = 18.5 °C], a relatively extended duration for a fish of this body size. This substantial lifespan, when compared to the age at first reproduction, underscores the species' potential for multiple reproductive events across its lifetime, a hallmark of iteroparous life histories. The slow pace of aging observed in captive individuals may reflect consistent food availability and the absence of predation pressure, factors that can significantly modulate senescence rates. In the wild, exposure to environmental stressors, territorial conflicts over nesting cavities, and predation by larger piscivores likely truncate the realized lifespan relative to this laboratory maximum. Nevertheless, the capacity for a nine-year life span provides ample opportunity for females to contribute to multiple breeding seasons.

Comparative analyses within the Batrachoididae reveal that the life history parameters of the Darkedge midshipman are broadly consistent with those of other nest-guarding teleosts. The ultimate total length for females, measured at 36 centimeters [Li = 36 centimeters], along with the maximum lifetime of 9 years [am = 9 years], positions this species toward the slower end of the life history continuum within its family at a temperature of 18.5 °C [T = 18.5 °C]. In contrast, the modest total length at puberty of 15.7 centimeters [Lp = 15.7 centimeters] indicates that reproductive maturity is achieved relatively early in the growth trajectory, a common pattern in fishes that experience high juvenile mortality. The wet weight at puberty of 40.5 grams [Wwp = 40.5 grams] represents only a fraction of the maximum adult body mass of 553 grams [Wwi = 553 grams], emphasizing the substantial scope for growth that remains after maturation. This combination of early maturity, extended longevity, and large adult body size fits a bet-hedging strategy in a variable coastal environment, where reproductive success depends on acoustic signaling, nest site availability, and paternal care.
